note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. No contest took place; the divisions listed were filled by sole nomination and the round is filed on the rural districts' polling day, Thursday 2 June 1927 (queue nominal 26 May). No nominations were received for Ballymacbrennan, Breda, Carryduff, Edenderry or Hillsborough, and the nomination for Maze was declared invalid. Three of the members deemed re-elected (Ballymacbrennan, Carryduff, Hillsborough) are recorded from the Lisburn Standard report of the council's annual meeting of 7 June 1927; Edenderry (Robert Thompson sat, but the 1924 return names John Thompson), Maze (the 1924 member, Joseph M'Candless, jun., is first seen again in January 1928) remain unnamed; Breda, whose 1924 co-opted member A. F. Blakely had died, was filled by co-opting James Dick on 7 June 1927, a co-option, not an election (Lisburn Standard, 10 June 1927, p. 3) (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 8 May 1924 return (Wm. John Johnston, J.P., Ballymacbrennan; Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924, p. 5); the Lisburn Standard meeting report cited names the member as sitting at the first meeting of the term, as he had through 1924-27 (e.g. Dromore Leader, 13 February 1926, p. 3). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
